apparatus_validity.notes: Bounded analytical self-phase; one exact theory artifact sealed; no code or GPU effect.

artifact_refs.provenance: Principal-authored bounded derivation of low-rank Fisher Anchor-GU, including error bounds, shadow-cost quantity, five quantitative predictions, and a fixed GPU1 falsification contract; no code or GPU effect.

counterevidence: Pinsker controls functionals on the anchor distribution, not arbitrary MU under distribution shift.
A rank<=8 sketch may fail to capture 90% Fisher trace, falsifying the near-free low-rank hypothesis.
The shuffled basis could perform similarly if improvements arise from generic step shrinkage rather than utility-aligned geometry.
Existing adaptive GU data show retain NLL is insufficient but do not establish that teacher-logit anchors are sufficient.
findings: Teacher-logit KL has zero first derivative at the original model, so a cached teacher KL cannot initially protect utility as a linear GU covector; the correct local authority is the Fisher/Gauss-Newton quadratic form.

A rank-r Fisher sketch yields an explicit drift bound with spectral residual epsilon_r and third-order remainder, enabling a low-rank ellipsoidal trust region rather than heuristic retain-NLL budgets.
The maximal safe step scale is the root of a scalar quadratic in low-rank anchor coordinates, so online runtime requires no teacher forward and only rank-r dot products.
For bounded anchor scores, Pinsker links a 0.05 functional tolerance to an interpretable anchor-KL budget B=0.005, conditional on top-k and distribution-mismatch residuals.
Forget-gradient overlap with the anchor subspace eta predicts shadow cost; low eta is the necessary condition for a nearly free utility anchor.
The fixed GPU1 experiment compares adaptive-safe, retain-only anchor, mixed general anchor, and shuffled-basis control on forget05 seed0 before any promotion.
